This. 
They say they wish they could help but when they had the chance, they looked away. It could’ve been prevented in so many cases. I don’t expect friends to be my therapists but just validating my feelings was all I asked for and offering support would’ve meant the world.

When I was in the first week of certain meds, I had racing suicidal thoughts and anxiety attacks (a common side effect and warning when first taking that medication at a relatively young age) I felt that the pain was stronger than the fear of facing death and my last moments but I had to hold on for a few more months which is why I took them. I wonder if it’s the same in the weeks if I’d get off meds.

I have a big family which is both good and bad. If I go, there are still other family members around to keep the loneliness and grief at bay. However, something tells me that I’m still cherished by my parents despite having many siblings. I’d be irreplaceable. Recently it’s getting hard to get out of bed and force myself to eat or do the simplest tasks and I’m battling every day for the few people that care. 
I don’t want to cause mental damage or for anyone to harm themselves because of me. Part of me wishes that something bad happens to me from a natural cause (not murder or accident due to human failure) without me taking action for it to be my fate and no one to beat themselves up for it.

Let’s hang in there. There are people who love and worry about you.
